newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee rebound sharply on arb, trade buying.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee rebound sharply on arb, trade buying.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures staged a strong rebound in late trade and prices ended sharply higher on arbitrage buying and trade short-covering, traders said.
"London has done quite well today," one said, adding that arbitrage buying in London against New York underpinned values.
"We've seen some arbitrage buying this afternoon as the arbitrage narrowed a bit this afternoon," he said.
Traders said gains were also lifted by trade short-covering as the market triggered some light buy stops at $1,530 basis December and $1,450 basis March.
By the finish, most-active January was $35 higher at $1,488 a tonne while front-month November firmed $29 at $1,549.
November's premium to January stayed at a strong $61 a tonne but the May/July premium widened to $25 from Tuesday's finish of $7. Volume reached 4,418 lots.
The improved sentiment was also helped by an early rally in New York as the market recovered from Tuesday's falls on a technical downward correction.
Traders noted no fresh news behind today's move but said that the persistent worries over near-term availabilities in the U.S. continued to provide some background support.

Keen robusta selling by Vietnam and Indonesia in the past weeks seemed to have abated this week as producers held back in view of surging prices, said one. -- Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
